why.cycleBudgetUsd: One budget for Vercel plus Neon in one billing cycle. The owner has not picked a number yet; 120 is the default. The cycle from 2026-10-12 was on course for about 41 dollars of Vercel and 54 dollars of Neon, about 95 in all, so 120 leaves about 25 dollars of room before it goes red.
why.vercel.cycleStartDay: Vercel bills from the 12th to the 11th: the Pro seat changes price on the charge day of the 12th (read 2026-11-12).
why.vercel.maxDailySpendUsd: Vercel effective cost for the whole team in one charge day. The 30 charge days from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-10 ran from 0.99 to 1.81 dollars, median 1.30. Three dollars is about 1.7 times the highest normal day; the flood days of 2026-08-30 to 2026-09-01 cost 7.84 to 10.69.
why.vercel.projects.1f3d9: Normal day for 1f3d9 CDN requests (Vercel renamed Edge Requests) and function invocations: the median of the 30 charge days from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-10 was about 180,000 of each, highest 239,680, lowest 81,377. The alarm goes red above 3 times this, 540,000, which no normal day reached and the 2.1 to 2.5 million a day flood of 2026-08-30 would.
why.neon.maxPreviewBranches: Eight leaves two places inside Neon's first ten branches for main and the protected preview/shared-vercel-testing.
why.neon.maxManualSnapshotsWithoutExpiry: Manual snapshots on the city project with no end date. Every production migration takes one and each is billed at about its full size every month. A cap of 10 plus one kept by name is arriving separately; 15 leaves room above it. Alert only, nothing is deleted.
